relevance_note: The paper is a case series of HA20 in three Chinese families and gives individual-level data for eight patients with TNFAIP3 variants ("Eight Chinese Han patients were diagnosed with HA20 in our department from 2018 to 2021").
method_note: Read the full text, Table 1 and the figure legends; no supplementary material is present. All spans were copied by hand from the Markdown and each one was checked character by character against the file. Where a row's status or evidence_basis repeats the feature, the same short quote is given again, because every non-missing value needs a span. Scope: the 8 patients with HA20 from the 3 families (P1, her mother and two sisters, P2, P2's daughter, P3, P3's daughter) plus the relatives the paper describes in relation to them (P2's aunt and two cousins, P3's mother and late maternal grandmother); the 126 patients of the literature review get no rows (publications.cohort_size_as_stated = 126). Labels: Table 1 shows patients as rows but the text uses its own labels, so the text labels (P1, P2, P3) are used for the probands; relatives without their own label are 'relation of <label>'; the two girls both called IV:1 are distinguished by '(Family n)'. Table 1 rows 2-4 (family 1) are three identical rows that cannot be assigned individually to the mother (IV:14) and the two sisters (V:22, V:26); the text identifies them and their features agree with those rows, so each of the three gets the same values. Their 'Age at onset' is printed as 'UN' and 'Age at diagnosis' as '>18' (a lower bound, not a number), so no ISO 8601 value was derived for either. Table symbols: the table notes define '+' as positive and '-' as negative, so '-' cells were recorded as excluded with that definition ('-, negative') quoted as a second span. No cell in Table 1 contains ' / ' stacked values. Contradictions found: (1) the Table 1 'Fever' column is discordant with the text for family 2 - the row with onset 9/diagnosis 12 (P2's daughter, text: 'recurrent fever') is 'Fever -', while the row with onset 15/diagnosis 35 (P2, text: 'without recurrent fever') is 'Fever +'; both phenotypic_features rows are emitted for each girl/mother and the checklist item 'recurrent fever' is 'not reported' for both; (2) P3's age at onset is 10 in the text but 15 in Table 1 - the text value is recorded and the discrepancy noted here; (3) P3 has 'positive anti-thyroglobulin (TG)'/'anti-thyroperoxidase (TPO)' antibodies but 'Blood tests for CBC, biochemistry panel, and autoantibodies were all normal.', so both rows are emitted and the checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' is 'not reported' for him; (4) for A547T the abstract states the variant was 'validated to be pathogenic in our study' while the Discussion states 'the accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown'. Variant-level fields: D-29 was applied strictly, so values stated only for the proband's variant are not copied to the relatives who carry the same variant (variant type is recorded for them because the paper states the class of the exact variant, e.g. 'missense mutation A547T', 'the splice site variant c.1906+2T>G'); the transcript 'NM_006290' printed for the Table 1 patients comes from the variants column header 'TNFAIP3 variations (NM_006290)', while P1's transcript NM_006290.4 is printed with her variant. Other notes: 'no ocular symptoms' with old uveitis on examination for P1 is recorded as an excluded row for ocular symptoms and the checklist item is 'observed'; the post-treatment statements for P1 ('she did not exhibit fever, arthralgia, oral ulcers, or eye discomfort after a year of treatment') were not treated as absences; P2's 'moderate anemia' is recorded as a phenotypic feature but was not mapped to the composite checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)', and P3's normal CBC likewise; P3's 'Henoch-Schonlein purpura' is recorded as a feature but was not mapped to the checklist item 'vasculitis'; the aunt and cousins of P2 'refused to do the gene testing', so they have no variant row and no clinical_diagnosis_basis; age_at_last_evaluation uses the ages printed for the patients at the time of the report (28-, 35- and 40-year-old, and the 13- and 10-year-old daughters).
